meta.title: About Rufaqaa — our story, vision and values
meta.description: The Rufaqaa story: from one charity's need to a global, open-source digital endowment. Our vision, mission, values, and the team behind the platform.

hero.title: The story of
hero.subtitle: What begins as one charity's need becomes, God willing, a digital endowment serving thousands of orphans around the world. This is how we started, and why we keep going.

story.title: From a local need,
story.lede: We didn't design Rufaqaa on a blank page — it was born from daily friction at a single charity, then grew because thousands of orphans needed the same answer.
story.phase1Desc: At one charity, orphan sponsorships were managed on scattered papers and spreadsheets. Transfers were logged by hand, and reports lagged by months. The need was clear: one transparent system serving everyone.
story.phase2Desc: Other partner charities saw the platform and asked to join, across several countries. Sponsors began reaching orphans across continents, and reports started flowing monthly, automatically.
story.phase3Desc: The final decision: no for-profit entity, no monopoly. Rufaqaa is an open-source digital endowment under the MIT license — any organization worldwide can use it free, copy it, or contribute to it. An unbroken good, God willing.

vm.title: Where we're headed,
vm.visionTitle: A world where no orphan is left without a companion.
vm.visionBody: We dream of a platform that connects every orphan — however far — with a sponsor who prays for them, checks on them, and becomes their companion. We dream of waiting lists disappearing, and sponsorship becoming as simple as sending a message.
vm.missionTitle: Connecting sponsors with orphans, transparently and with dignity.
vm.missionBody: We build an open-source, secure, easy-to-use tool that lets any verified charity manage its sponsorships efficiently, and lets any sponsor follow their orphan with confidence — without ever compromising the child's dignity or privacy.

values.title: Four values
values.titleAccent: we answer for before the numbers
values.lede: Values aren't slogans on a wall — they're decision criteria. Facing any design or financial choice, we ask: does it serve sincerity? Transparency? Dignity? Excellence?
values.v1Desc: Deeds are judged by intentions. We work seeking God's pleasure — not reputation or awards. When intention conflicts with interest, we choose intention.
values.v2Desc: The code is open, the accounts are audited, the decisions are documented. Every amount carries a serial number — from the sponsor's card to the hand that delivers it to the orphan.
values.v3Desc: An orphan is a whole human being, not a marketing case. No real photos, no tear-jerking stories to extract donations. We guard privacy as we guard money.
values.v4Desc: God loves that when one of you does a thing, they do it well. We build the platform with care — every line of code, every button, every word placed deliberately.

hadith.title: A hadith
hadith.text: I and the guardian of the orphan will be in Paradise like this
hadith.source: Sahih al-Bukhari · The merit of one who cares for an orphan
hadith.narrator: Narrated by Sahl ibn Sa'd (may God be pleased with him)
hadith.tafsir: The Prophet ﷺ joined his index and middle fingers, indicating that the guardian of an orphan will be this close to him on the Day of Judgement. Guardianship isn't only financial support — it includes care, supplication, and following up on the orphan's education, health and character. The Prophet ﷺ made it general, opening the door for every believer to attain this merit.

os.title: Why we chose to be
os.lede: In charitable work, trust is the currency. Open code is the strongest form of trust — because you don't take our word for it, you read it yourself.
os.point1: Full transparency — every line of code is open to public review. Any developer or security engineer can verify for themselves how data is stored and transactions are protected.
os.point2: Any organization can use it free — no subscription fees, no dependence on Rufaqaa as a company. Download, deploy, modify — freely, under the MIT license.
os.point3: Community contributions — developers, translators and reviewers from several countries have contributed code and translations. A good not limited to one team.
os.point4: An unbroken endowment — even if the founding team stopped tomorrow, the code remains available forever for any party to complete or copy. An ongoing charity in software form.

meta.title: How it works — Rufaqaa from the inside
meta.description: A detailed, step-by-step explanation of how Rufaqaa works: for sponsors, for orphans and their families, and for partner organizations — with the full money flow and security safeguards.

hero.title: Rufaqaa
hero.subtitle: Simple on the outside, precise in operation. Here we explain step by step how your sponsorship reaches your orphan — and how the platform verifies every amount and every report.

donors.title: For sponsors — how do you sponsor an orphan?
donors.subtitle: Five steps stand between you and becoming an orphan's companion. The first three take minutes; the rest continue with you as long as you wish.
donors.metaLabel: to register and make the first payment
donors.s1Desc: No registration or email needed — open the 'Browse orphans' page and you'll find profiles of orphans available for sponsorship now, with age, country, and education status.
donors.s2Title: Choose an orphan who touches your heart
donors.s2Desc: Each orphan has a profile with their story — without personal photos — to help you choose. You can sponsor one orphan or more, in different countries.
donors.s3Desc: Payment options: Visa/Mastercard, Apple Pay, K-NET, or bank transfer. Every transaction is encrypted, and a PDF receipt reaches you instantly. Sponsorship is monthly and automatic, and you can cancel anytime.
donors.s4Desc: Each month, you receive a report approved by the partner organization: health status, schooling, the orphan's activities — with safe images and official documents. The report is reviewed before it reaches you.
donors.s5Title: Message the guardian if you wish
donors.s5Desc: You can send messages to the orphan's guardian through the platform — and every message passes human review before delivery, protecting both sides. The guardian doesn't get your data, nor you theirs.

orphansPath.title: For orphans & guardians — how does support arrive?
orphansPath.subtitle: You and your orphan don't deal with the platform directly — everything goes through the accredited charity in your country. It is your face to us.
orphansPath.s1Desc: Direct yourself or the guardian to the nearest accredited partner — a locally licensed charity. They open a file with the official documents and a social report.
orphansPath.s2Desc: The partner manager reviews the file, then submits it to Rufaqaa for approval. An orphan's profile isn't shown to sponsors before document verification is complete.
orphansPath.s3Title: The orphan is matched with a sponsor
orphansPath.s3Desc: The orphan's profile appears to a potential sponsor — via direct browsing or a marketing campaign. When the sponsor chooses them, matching happens instantly and the sponsorship counter starts.
orphansPath.s4Title: Monthly disbursement from the partner's account
orphansPath.s4Desc: Rufaqaa transfers the total of sponsorships to the partner's account in one batch each month. The partner then disburses to the guardian per its policy, and a receipt is signed.
orphansPath.s5Title: Periodic reports uploaded to the platform
orphansPath.s5Desc: A partner staff member uploads a monthly report on the orphan: health, schooling, exceptional needs, and images under privacy controls. Reports pass review before reaching the sponsor.

partnersPath.title: For partner organizations — how do you join?
partnersPath.subtitle: Rufaqaa can't work without you. The partner is the local eye and the hand that reaches the orphan. But we are careful in choosing.
partnersPath.s1Desc: The organization fills a partnership request with name, country, license, expected number of orphans, and bank accounts — and uploads document copies electronically.
partnersPath.s2Desc: The platform reviews the documents with an independent auditor in the organization's country. Review covers license validity, activity history, and community reputation.
partnersPath.s3Desc: The organization gets manager and staff accounts. Staff start registering orphans via 'Register new orphan': a full profile plus documents, submitted for the manager's approval.
partnersPath.s4Desc: The organization receives a unified bank transfer for all its sponsored orphans from the prior month, with a statement listing each orphan and amount (without sponsor contact data).
partnersPath.s5Desc: The organization disburses to guardians per its policy and obtains a documented receipt signature. Staff then upload the receipt plus a monthly report on each orphan's status.

flow.title: Where does
flow.lede: Five stops between your card and your orphan's hand. Every stop is documented with a serial number, and audited by a neutral party annually.
flow.note1Desc: for every payment transaction, and card data is never stored with us.
flow.note2Desc: 24–48 hours from payment until the amount reaches the partner's account monthly.
flow.note3Desc: by an independent chartered accounting firm, with results published on the transparency page.
flow.note4Desc: 95% of the amount reaches the orphan directly, 3% operations, 2% reserves.

security.title: How do we protect
security.lede: Not just secure infrastructure — a whole approach to platform design that puts the child's dignity before any marketing feature.
security.c1Desc: Payment data is encrypted with TLS 1.3, and orphan data is encrypted in the database with managed keys.
security.c2Desc: No full family names, no clear face photos, and no orphan contact data available to the sponsor. A 'minimum necessary' principle.
security.c3Desc: An independent chartered accounting firm audits the accounts and operations every 12 months, with results published publicly on the transparency page.
security.c4Desc: All code is on GitHub under the MIT license. Any security expert can review encryption, storage and data handling for themselves.

faq.title: Answers
faq.lede: We've gathered the most common questions here — organized by category. Browse by topic.
faq.g1a1: The minimum varies by country based on the orphan's actual need. Generally, the average ranges between 15 and 50 Kuwaiti dinars per month (or the equivalent in your currency). The actual amount appears on each orphan's profile before sponsorship.
faq.g1q2: Can I cancel the sponsorship anytime?
faq.g1a2: Yes, you can cancel from your account anytime with no obligation or fees. We just let you know that your orphan will return to the list, and that if the reason is temporary financial difficulty you can pause for a month instead of cancelling permanently.
faq.g1q3: When does the sponsorship reach the orphan?
faq.g1a3: From your card to Rufaqaa: instantly via MyFatoorah. From Rufaqaa to the partner: 24–48 hours as a bank transfer. From the partner to the guardian: within 5–10 days of the next month's start. The whole process is at most two weeks from the payment date.
faq.g1q4: Do you provide a zakat receipt?
faq.g1a4: Yes, we provide an annual receipt you can download from your account — with the total of your yearly donations and transfer numbers. Tax-exemption rules vary by country, so consult the relevant specialists in your country.
faq.g2q1: Is the platform secure? How do you protect my data?
faq.g2a1: Yes — we use TLS 1.3 encryption for all transactions, and encryption for data in the database. We never store card numbers — they go directly to MyFatoorah, which holds PCI-DSS certification. The code is open on GitHub for anyone to verify.
faq.g2q2: What are MyFatoorah's fees? Are they deducted from the sponsorship?
faq.g2a2: MyFatoorah charges between 2.5% and 3% depending on the payment method. These fees are covered by the operations share (3%) — your sponsorship reaches the orphan in full.
faq.g2q3: How do I know my sponsorship actually reached the orphan?
faq.g2a3: You receive a PDF receipt instantly after payment, then notifications at each stage: the amount reaching the partner, delivery to the guardian with a signed receipt, and the orphan's report at month's end. Every transaction has a traceable serial number.
faq.g2q4: Can I contact the orphan or guardian directly?
faq.g2a4: Yes, but through the platform only — no direct contact. Every message passes human review before delivery to protect both sides. The guardian doesn't get your contact data, nor you theirs.
faq.g3a1: A licensed chartered accounting firm, financially and administratively independent from Rufaqaa's management, audits the accounts annually, with audit results published on the transparency page.
faq.g3q2: Where do I see the full financial reports?
faq.g3a2: On the transparency page — you'll find audited annual reports as soon as they're issued, plus live numbers on sponsored orphans and countries served.
faq.g3q3: Is the project for-profit? How much does the Rufaqaa team earn?
faq.g3a3: The project is not for-profit — it's a digital endowment. No one on the team takes a salary. The 3% operations share is spent only on servers, payment-gateway fees, and the auditor's fees.
faq.g4q1: Do I need an account to browse orphans?
faq.g4a1: No — browsing orphans is available without an account. You only need an account when starting a sponsorship, to link the payment to your account and receive reports.
faq.g4q2: Do you have a mobile app?
faq.g4a2: The platform is optimized for mobile via the browser. iOS and Android apps are on the roadmap.
faq.g4q3: How do I contribute to the code or report a bug?
faq.g4a3: We welcome any contribution! Start from the repository on GitHub and read the CONTRIBUTING file. For bugs, open a new Issue; for features, start a Discussion.
